item.title: Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua full fight card announced
item.description: The full fight card for Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) vs. Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) has been formally announced. The announcement was made on Wednesday over social media . Fight fans around the world will be able to watch those bouts on The Ring magazine’s social media accounts and Netflix’s TikTok. Fury vs. Joshua headlines a Dec. 11 card promoted by Queensberry Promotions, Matchroom Boxing, and Sela. Fight fans around the world will be able to catch that bout and three other undercard clashes live on Netflix. Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua full fight card Fight fans may already be familiar with some of the bouts that are scheduled to take place on this card. The undercard that will be broadcast on Netflix consists of three heavyweight clashes. Deontay Wilder (45-4-1, 43 KOs) is set to take on Martin Bakole (21-2-1, 16 KOs). Moses Jolly (12-0-1, 8 KOs) takes on Igor Macedo (15-1, 14 KOs) while Da’Mazion Vanhouter (14-0, 11 KOs) faces Michael Essomba (11-2, 10 KOs). Below are the fights that will be on broadcast on social media: Joe Cordina vs. Mauricio Lara, lightweight Hayato Tsutsumi vs. Vic Pasillas, featherweight Reito Tsutsumi vs. Muheeb Fazeldin, super featherweight Constantino Nanga vs. Lerrone Richards, light heavyweight Mikie Tallon vs. Sean Bruce, super flyweight Mohammed Alakel vs. Rogger Rivera, super featherweight Odel Kamara vs. Patrik Matejcek, super welterweight Roman Fury vs. Adam Kolarik, heavyweight Mark Robinson/Goldstar Promotions The Big Fight Weekend verdict One fight that stands out among the eight that were announced on Wednesday is the one between Cordina and Lara. Both are former world champions and relatively better known than many of the other fighters on the undercard. There is also the clash between Tsutsumi and Pasillas, a fight that sees a talented youngster take on a veteran of the sport. Tallon takes a step up in opposition against Bruce, a former British flyweight champion. With all that being said, it feels like quantity has been valued over quality when it comes to this fight card. Fazeldin spent nearly six years out of the ring before returning earlier this year and yet finds himself facing someone like Tsutsumi. Alakel will be having his tenth bout as a professional, yet takes on an opponent who is 3-7 while Roman Fury faces a 10-12 fighter. It really does seem like the organizers put more care in making Fury vs. Joshua happen and neglected to put competitive fights on the undercard. On Dec. 11, fight fans can only hope that the bouts are more competitive than they look. item.title: ‘I talked to him’ – Andoni Iraola shares injury update on Victor Munoz after Brugge ‘pain’
item.description: ‘I talked to him’ – Andoni Iraola shares injury update on Victor Munoz after Brugge ‘pain’ Andoni Iraola has shared an update on the injury sustained by Victor Munoz in Liverpool’s win over Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The only blemish on a terrific result for the Reds in Belgium was the sight of the Spanish winger hobbling off towards the end of the first half, appearing to hurt his knee when overstretching to try and keep the ball after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area. A stretcher had been readied for the 23-year-old, but he was at least able to pick himself up off the ground and leave the pitch flanked by medical staff. Iraola shares ‘optimistic’ injury update on Munoz Speaking to reporters after the match, Iraola gave an update on Munoz’s injury, with Liverpool’s number 23 due to go for an assessment to verify the seriousness of the issue. The Reds’ head coach said (via liverpoolfc.com ): “It is the worst part of the game, definitely. He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished. “It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… but obviously it’s very early to tell if there is something more than the knock. “In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.” (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Fingers crossed for good news on Munoz The initial signs from Munoz certainly weren’t good, with the winger on the ground for a few minutes before managing to pick himself up, but this update from Iraola at least paints a slightly better picture for now. We still have to wait for the outcome of the assessment that he’s due to undergo today before we know how severe the injury is, and how long he’s expected to be out of action. We can only hope that it isn’t a serious setback for the 23-year-old, who’s looked bright and effervescent in his performances for Liverpool so far and was rewarded with a rare start last night before the unfortunate body blow. Munoz had been playing well in Brugge, too, with Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle noting how the Spaniard offered a ‘real threat with his pace and a regular outlet down the right’ until he was forced off in the 42nd minute. Fingers crossed for good news on the winger once the medical assessment is completed.

item.title: Chiefs hold edge over Bills in one area that could prove telling
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs hold an edge over the Buffalo Bills in one key area as the two teams get set for their titanic Thanksgiving game. The Chiefs come into the game as one of the least penalized teams through 11 weeks of play. Kansas City players have been flagged just 64 times this season, with the majority of penalties (offensive holding) meant to protect quarterback Patrick Mahomes. That's good enough to rank Kansas City 28th in the NFL for penalties, with only four teams flagged fewer times.. The Bills are among the most flagged teams (6th) with 83 penalties. Buffalo ranks 2nd in the league and are first in defensive holding calls. Head coach Joe Brady has said he wants to reduce pre-snap penalties. "The pre-snap penalties, it's embarrassing," Brady said last week after a Jets game that saw nine pre-snap penalties with seven accepted. The Bills have been flagged 18 times for false starts; the Chiefs have been flagged just four times. Yes, the Bills are 9-1 on the season, but against the 8-2 Chiefs, giving Kansas City an advantage could prove costly. item.title: The Bills’ wild Thanksgiving history goes back more than 60 years
item.description: When the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving Night, it will be their 12th appearance on America’s favorite football holiday and just their seventh since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger. During their heyday in the American Football League, the Bills were a fixture on the Thanksgiving football smorgasbord as they played five times in a span of eight years, more than any other AFL team. But after being largely ignored for about a half century - the Bills are back to being the darlings of Thanksgiving as this will be their fourth appearance in the last seven years. While the Lions and Dallas Cowboys have hosted Thanksgiving Day NFL games on an almost yearly basis, Detroit since 1934, Dallas since 1966, there was no designated franchise that played host to a Thanksgiving game during the 10-year lifespan of the AFL between 1960-69. There were 13 turkey day games played in the AFL and they were hosted by the Kansas City Chiefs (3), San Diego Chargers (3), Oakland Raiders (2), New York Titans (2), Denver Broncos (2), and Houston Oilers (1). The league wasn’t interested in playing a national game at Buffalo’s decrepit War Memorial Stadium, especially in late November, but it was fine with scheduling the Bills as the road team against New York in 1961, San Diego in 1964 and 1965, and Oakland in 1966 and 1968. Until this recent run of games, the only three times the Bills had played on Thanksgiving since the merger, they were again on the road, beating St. Louis in 1975 and losing to Detroit in 1976 and 1994. Here is a summary of the 11 previous Bills’ Thanksgiving Day games: Nov. 23, 1961 — Titans 21, Bills 14 Not a good day for the Bills’ offensive line which allowed 10 sacks for a total of 78 yards, the last coming in the final seconds with Buffalo facing fourth-and-goal from the New York 9. Quarterback M.C. item.description: AUCKLAND, NEW ZEALAND - NOVEMBER 26: City Kickboxing head trainer Eugene Bareman addresses the media on November 26, 2026 in Auckland, New Zealand in relation to fighters Navajo Stirling (L) and Carlos Ulberg (R) who both train together out of the Auckland based gym. (Photo by Dean Purcell/New Zealand Herald via Getty Images) Surging Light Heavyweight knockout artist Navajo Stirling has earned a UFC title shot … if he wants it. The 29-year-old Kiwi won four bouts this year, extending his undefeated record to 12-0 with seven of those victories coming inside the Octagon. Not only is Stirling winning, but he’s knocking out opponents left and right, including a pair of former champions in Jan Blachowicz and Jiri Prochazka (watch here) . Young and hungry, he’s clearly the most deserving 205-pound contender at the moment. Unfortunately, his teammate Carlos Ulberg already holds the crown. After stopping “BJP,” Stirling sounded hesitant to face his training partner, who also knocked out Prochazka earlier this year. However, the door was at least still open to some degree. City Kickboxing head coach, Eugene Bareman, made a public address with the clear intention of shutting down these conversations. Flanked by both Stirling and Ulberg, Bareman resolutely declared that City Kickboxing athletes will never fight one another. “The status at the moment is, and it’s been like this forever, is the boys from the same gym don’t fight,” Bareman explained (via Yahoo ). “We’ve had that agreement from the very onset of this gym when it first started, that if you join this team, you’ve got to commit to not fighting each other. item.description: Roma star personally urges Real Madrid youngster to join Italian side in January: ‘Come, come’ Real Madrid face a difficult decision in the January transfer window regarding the future of talented Brazilian youngster Endrick. The 20-year-old is widely regarded as one of the biggest attacking talents of his generation, but opportunities in the Spanish capital have been few and far between. Despite manager Jose Mourinho repeatedly expressing his full confidence in Endrick’s abilities, the lack of minutes is making it difficult to justify those words. Interest from European clubs is certainly not a problem for Endrick. Ahead of January, Italian clubs are keeping a close eye . Wesley confirms attempts to convince Endrick Now, AS Roma defender and international teammate Wesley has admitted that he has already spoken to Endrick about joining Roma. Speaking to TNT Sports after the Serie A side’s impressive 2-2 Champions League draw against PSG, Wesley admitted that Roma would love to sign the Los Blancos starlet. Wesley Franca wants Endrick at Roma. (Photo by Timothy Rogers/Getty Images) “I gave him a little nudge. I told him, ‘Come, come,’ but he’s the one who decides. It’s his career,” the defender explained. The Brazilian also made it clear that Endrick would receive a warm welcome should he eventually decide to join Roma. “I hope that wherever he goes, or if he stays at Real Madrid, he is very happy and successful because he’s a good kid who deserves it.” “If he comes, he’ll certainly be very well received by Roma’s supporters and by us,” Wesley added. Mourinho remains reluctant to sanction a departure Roma’s interest in the 20-year-old is not exactly new, with the Italian club having previously explored a loan move for him. However, securing his signature in January could prove difficult. Mourinho remains firmly opposed to the idea of Endrick leaving mid-season. Endrick is unable to get regular minutes at Real Madrid. (Photo by David Balogh/Getty Images) The Portuguese manager has always maintained that he believes Endrick could have a much more prominent role to play in the latter part of the season. However, with Carlos Espi ahead of him in the striker pecking order and the Spaniard himself struggling for minutes, the situation doesn’t look great for Endrick. If Real Madrid ultimately decide to let Endrick leave, it’s likely to be on a loan deal similar to the one with Olympique Lyon back in January. Endrick still has a lot of potential and the talent to succeed at the Spanish club, and it remains to be seen what decision the club makes in the winter transfer window.

item.title: Kenny Smith makes Luka Doncic point to stress what LeBron James does to put ‘NBA in danger’
item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images LeBron James has turned over a new leaf in his NBA career by leaving behind Luka Doncic and the Lakers, but Kenny Smith says what he keeps doing has put the NBA in danger. Both Luka Doncic and LeBron James are enjoying their time in the NBA despite going their separate ways with the Philadelphia 76ers and the Los Angeles Lakers. James is turning back Father Time, while Doncic is relishing added responsibilities with the Lakers and thriving with it. After James’ latest triple-double in the 76ers’ victory, Kenny Smith made a Doncic point to stress that what James is doing puts the “NBA in danger”. Kenny Smith on LeBron James The 76ers beat the Miami Heat in the NBA Cup group stage, and James reminded everyone that he’s still a force to be reckoned with at age 41. He put up 25 points, 10 rebounds, and 12 assists, finally finding his 3PT range in the process as well, to finish with the highest +/- among all the starters. Smith, speaking on Inside the NBA , said after the game that people shouldn’t be surprised at what James keeps doing, because he did it last season as well. James just manages his minutes and picks and chooses when to go full-tilt, and when he does, it’s game over for the opposition. To have that kind of an impact on a winning team that is a championship contender is a remarkable ode to his fitness and professionalism. item.description: Aaron Rodgers has thrown 16 touchdown passes and six interceptions from 10 games this season [Getty Images] Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. In a brief statement published on Wednesday afternoon local time, the Steelers announced Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, was no longer with the franchise. That came after a tumultuous 24 hours, which began with the Steelers announcing at 23:10 local time on Tuesday that Rodgers had been replaced as their starting quarterback. He then appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, saying he would not rejoin the team. "That ship has sailed," said Rodgers, who turns 43 next week. During the 34-minute interview, he was critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, including accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings. They won the Super Bowl together with the Green Bay Packers in 2011 and, during Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Rodgers claims that McCarthy ended the half-time huddle with a chant of "one, two, three, Packers". McCarthy, 63, was in charge for most of Rodgers' 18-year spell with the Packers and left in 2018. He then coached the Dallas Cowboys from 2020-2024. Tension had developed between the pair over play-calling and Rodgers says he told McCarthy "try to bench me or don't change the play-caller, then you should just release me". Shortly before Pittsburgh confirmed his release, McCarthy responded to Rodgers' interview, telling reporters "there was an ultimatum made that was clearly outside his job description", adding it was his decision to let the player go. All this came after the Steelers said that Mason Rudolph will start Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos and that Rodgers would be inactive, so would not serve as back-up to the 31-year-old. Rodgers, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 after two years with the New York Jets, was "99% sure" he was going to retire after leading the Steelers to last season's play-offs. McCarthy's appointment persuaded him to play one more year but Rodgers told the talk show on Wednesday the season had not been "what I signed up for". Although the Steelers have a 6-4 record, they have had two straight defeats after losing 19-16 at Philadelphia on Sunday. Analysis - an unceremonious end to an illustrious career? Pittsburgh's brief statement confirming Rodgers' release is likely the unceremonious end to an illustrious career. While Rodgers was unable to claim a second Super Bowl win with Green Bay, he was named the season MVP in 2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021. Only Peyton Manning (five) has won the award more times. item.description: FBL-FRA-LIGUE1-NICE-PSG - AFP Luis Enrique admitted AS Roma handed Paris Saint-Germain their toughest test of the season after Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw snapped PSG's 12-game winning streak. Following Donyell Malen's late penalty, the Spanish coach lavished praise on Gian Piero Gasperini and even tipped the Italian side to win the Scudetto. Roma end PSG's 12-game winning streak Enrique praised Roma for delivering his side's toughest test of the season after Wednesday's 2-2 Champions League draw . The result snapped PSG's impressive 12-game winning streak across all competitions. Roma striker Malen secured a share of the points in the 78th minute, blasting home a decisive penalty. It marked the first time PSG had dropped points since losing at home to Monaco on September 4. Enrique hails Roma's mentality and attitude Rather than dwelling on the end of his team's dominant run, Enrique was quick to credit the visitors for pushing his players to their limits. "Without any doubt this was our toughest match of this season, in the Champions League or the French league," Enrique said, as quoted by ESPN . "I am happy with the result, and the merit goes to Roma. Facing a team with this attitude and this kind of mentality is very hard to play against. It's very different to the kind of match we're used to." Respect for Gasperini's tactical setup Wednesday's clash also marked the first time Enrique had gone head-to-head with Roma boss Gasperini in the dugout. The Spaniard paused and nodded in respect when discussing his counterpart's tactical setup. "It's the first time I've come up against him as a coach," Luis Enrique said. "It's better to talk about Roma's future, not PSG's. Roma's future is wonderful, they can win the Scudetto. Champions League league phase standings and outlook The draw leaves PSG's position in the Champions League league phase unchanged. item.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
item.description: Jannik Sinner is a five-time Grand Slam champion [Getty Images] Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee. The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. In a social media post on Tuesday, world number two Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO [Australian Open] in January following his recent surgery," said Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon." The 2027 Australian Open main draw starts on 17 January. Sinner's challenge at the 2026 tournament was ended by a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic. Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way. However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title. Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece. He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025. Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking. item.title: Why the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend could be doomed to fail
item.description: It is the season of feasting, of plates piled high, of over-indulgence in the name of festive excess and collective conviviality. How much is too much? That is a question that may well be answered on the inaugural Nations Championship finals weekend, with a six-course tasting menu of global flavour whetting just about any appetite. The Twickenham grounds staff may not give thanks – even if there is a new pitch for the super-sized portions to be served – but for any rugby lover prone to immoderation, the larder is stocked for three days of gluttony. The world’s top 12 nations will take to the same surface in an ambitious array of Test matches that stretch from Friday afternoon to Sunday evening; this sport has not really known anything quite like it. All 12 teams will play at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham over three days on Nations Championship Finals weekend (Reuters) “It is amazing,” the South Africa rugby captain Siya Kolisi beamed at a chaotic launch on Wednesday as he looked ahead to a final with France. “It gives a different feeling for it because you know you’re fighting for something. Every game is important, but I think this has been really amazing because you’re competing against the north, but you’re also competing against the south in the same pools. “I think it has given it more drive and it has given it more excitement. I think it’s great to finally get that, the two best teams from the two hemispheres playing against each other.” Siya Kolisi is excited for the Nations Championship final (Getty) Will it be a success? The jury is out; so, too, are a significant number of potential match-goers. One can, if that way inclined and prepared to pay a pretty penny, still buy tickets to each and every day, with the top tier of the Allianz Stadium expected to be shut off entirely for Friday’s double-header. There may multiple mitigating factors, with England having just sold out three home games and fans elsewhere in Europe having had recent opportunity to watch their teams on home soil – but for a competition designed to grow the commercial potential of the sport, it is an inauspicious start. The format does not help matters, with fixtures only confirmed late last Saturday, hardly providing consumer certainty.
